<h>Hymnus</h>
<c>V</c>írginis Proles, Opiféxque Matris,
Virgo quem gessit, peperítque Virgo:
Vírginis festum cánimus trophǽum
Accipe votum.

<h>H</h>æc tua Virgo dúplici beáta
Sorte, dum gestit frágilem domáre
Córporis sexum, dómuit cruéntum
Corpóre sæclum.

<h>U</h>nde nec mortem, nec amíca mortis
Sæva pœnárum génera pavéscens,
Sánguine fuso méruit sacrátum
Scándere cælum.

Parce jam culpis, vítia remíttens,
Quo tibi puri resonémus almum
Péctoris hymnum.

Et tibi compar utriúsque semper
Spíritus alme, Deus unus, omni

b.1d2384938a:
<h>Hymn</h>
<c>S</c>on of a virgin, maker of thy mother,
Thou, rod and blossom from a stem unstainèd,
While we a Virgin's triumphs are rehearsing,
Hear our petition!

<h>L</h>o, on thy handmaid fell a two-fold blessing,
Who, in her body vanquishing the weakness,
In that same body, grace from heaven obtaining,
Bore the world witness.

<h>D</h>eath, nor the rending pains of death appalled her;
Bondage and torment found her undefeated:
So by the shedding of her blood attained she
Heavenly guerdon.

<h>F</h>ountain of mercy, hear the prayers she offers;
Purge our offences, pardon our transgressions,
So that hereafter we to thee may render
Praise with thanksgiving.

<h>T</h>hou, the All-Father, thou, the One-Begotten,
Thou, Holy Spirit, Three in One co-equal,
Glory be henceforth thine through all the ages,
World without ending.
Amen.

<h>Lectio 3</h>
<c>C</c>atharína, nóbilis virgo Alexandrína, liberálium ártium stúdia cum fídei ardóre coniúngens, cum multos Christiános Maximíni jussu ad supplícium rapi vidéret, ipsum ádiit Maximínum, eíque Christi fidem ad salútem esse necessáriam strénue affirmávit. Ejus prudéntiam admirátus, tyránnus retinéri eam jubet; et, accersítis úndique doctíssimis homínibus, ei persuadére studet, ut ad idolórum cultum se convértat. Sed contra áccidit; plures enim ex iis viris, sapientíssimis ratiónibus a Catharína convícti, Christi fidem sunt ampléxi et pro ea mori non dubitárunt. Quam ob rem Maximínus blandítiis primum, deínde torméntis Catharínam de senténtia dedúcere aggréditur; sed, cum nihil profíceret, eam secúri pércuti ímperat.

<h>Reading 3</h>
<c>C</c>atherine was a noble virgin of Alexandria who united a zeal for the liberal arts with an ardent faith. When she saw many Christians given up to torture by Maximin, she went to him and strongly stated the necessity of faith in Christ for salvation. Wondering at her wisdom, the tyrant commanded her to be held, and, assembling the most learned men from all sides, he tried to persuade her to turn to the worship of idols. But the opposite happened; many of those men were convinced by Catherine's wise reasoning and embraced the faith of Christ and did not hesitate to die for it. Because of this, Maximin tried promises first and then threats to win Catherine from her conviction; but, when nothing succeeded, he had her beheaded with an axe.

<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>N</c>ovember 26th 2027, the 27th day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Fabriano, in the March of Ancona, the blessed Abbot Silvester, founder of the Congregation of Monks of the Order of St Benedict, who are called Silvestrians.
<h>A</h>t Alexandria, the holy martyr Peter, Pope of that city, a man enriched with all graces, who was beheaded by order of the Emperor Galerius Maximian.
<h>L</h>ikewise at Alexandria, in the same persecution, the holy martyrs Faustus a Priest, Didius, and Ammonius, along with whom are commemorated the Egyptian Bishops Phileas, Hesychius, Pachomius, and Theodore, and six hundred and sixty Others, who were raised to heaven by the sword of the persecutor.
<h>A</h>t the village called Fratta, in the territory of Rovigo, (in the year 1149,) the holy martyr Bellinus, Bishop of Padua, who, being a stout defender of the rights of the Church, was cruelly set upon by assassins and slain with many wounds.
<h>A</h>t Nicomedia, the holy Priest Marcellus, who in the time of the Emperor Constantius was thrown over a cliff by the Arians, and so died a martyr.
<h>A</h>t Rome, (at the end of the fourth century,) the holy Confessor Pope Siricius, very famous for his teaching, godliness, and zeal for the faith. He condemned diverse heretics and restored the discipline of the Church by healthy enactments.
<h>A</h>t Autun, (in the third century,) holy Amator, Bishop (of that see.)
<h>A</h>t Constance, (in the tenth century,) holy Conrad, Bishop (of that see.)
<h>A</h>t Rome, (in the year 1751,) the holy Confessor Leonard of Port Maurice, of the Order of Friars Minor of the stricter observance, who was famous for his zeal for the salvation of souls and his holy journeys throughout Italy, and whose name the Supreme Pontiff Pius IX enrolled among those of the Saints.
<h>I</h>n the country of Rheims, (in the seventh century,) the holy Confessor Basolus.
<h>A</h>t Adrianople, in Paphlagonia, the holy hermit Stylian, who was famous for miracles.
<h>I</h>n Armenia, (in the tenth century,) the holy monk Nicon.

<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<c>t</c>o Matthew
<r>Matt 25:1-13.</r>
<c>A</c>t that time Jesus spoke this parable to His disciples: “Then will the kingdom of heaven be like ten virgins who took their lamps and went forth to meet the bridegroom and the bride. Five of them were foolish and five wise. But the five foolish, when they took their lamps, took no oil with them, while the wise did take oil in their vessels with the lamps. Then as the bridegroom was long in coming, they all became drowsy and slept. And at midnight a cry arose, 'Behold, the bridegroom is coming, go forth to meet him!' Then all those virgins arose and trimmed their lamps. And the foolish said to the wise, 'Give us some of your oil, for our lamps are going out.' The wise answered, saying, 'Lest there may not be enough for us and for you, go rather to those who sell it, and buy some for yourselves.' Now while they were gone to buy it, the bridegroom came; and those who were ready went in with him to the marriage feast, and the door was shut. Finally there came also the other virgins, who said, 'Sir, sir, open the door for us!' But he answered and said, 'Amen I say to you, I do not know you.' Watch therefore, for you know neither the day nor the hour.”
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
